messages:
ashok patel: Heads-up — we're seeing intermittent pod-to-pod packet loss and huge p95 latencies for GRPC between GPU pods in us-west-2 (dedicated pool). Raising here before it pages.
maria chen: Which AZs and are these on the new NIC firmware hosts?
ashok patel: AZ a/b, ded-gpu-az-a-{0..3} and ded-gpu-az-b-{0..3}. NIC fw is mixed; ~30% on 1.2.3 (new) others on 1.2.1. Interesting thing: IPv4 traffic looks fine, IPv6 inter-pod flows are dropping.
taylor nguyen: Hmm. Any tcpdump / neigh traces?
ashok patel: tcpdump snippet (pod src -> pod dst):
```
18:31:12.123456 IP6 fe80::abcd > fe80::1234: ICMP6, neighbor solicitation, who has 2001:db8:10::12? lladdr: fa:16:3e:xx:xx:xx
18:31:12.123457 IP6 fe80::1234 > fe80::abcd: ICMP6, neighbor advertisement, tgt lladdr fa:16:3e:yy:yy:yy (solicited)
18:31:12.500000 IP6 fe80::abcd > fe80::dead: ICMP6, neighbor solicitation, who has 2001:db8:10::12? lladdr: fa:16:3e:xx:xx:xx
# retransmits then connection stalls
```
ashok patel: On the node where app complained, `ip -6 neigh show` shows two entries for the same IPv6 pod IP tied to different ifaces (vxlan0 and eth0) and one is STALE, one is REACHABLE. Looks like neighbor cache shadowing.
```
$ ip -6 neigh show | grep 2001:db8:10::12
2001:db8:10::12 dev vxlan0 lladdr fa:16:3e:aa:aa:aa REACHABLE
2001:db8:10::12 dev eth0 lladdr fa:16:3e:bb:bb:bb STALE
```
maria chen: That explains asymmetric path — kernel choosing the wrong iface for egress. Are we running proxy_ndp or any host-proxy features?
ashok patel: sysctl shows proxy_ndp=0 across the board:
```
$ sysctl net.ipv6.conf.all.proxy_ndp
net.ipv6.conf.all.proxy_ndp = 0
```
jin park: We use Cilium with host-routes + direct-node-routes. There's a known edge-case where kube-proxy/host-network services + host aliases cause duplicated neighbor learning when pods are moved and vxlan tunnels still have stale entries.
taylor nguyen: Could also be split-horizon from our BGP/RR config on the ToR. If the ToR is proxying NDP for some prefixes and hosts are also learning via local tunnel, neighbor entries can be inconsistent.
ashok patel: I hit a mitigation: on one node I forced flush of the stale neighbor and then set `ip -6 route add 2001:db8:10::12/128 dev vxlan0`. That fixed routing for that pod; GRPC p95 dropped from 450ms -> 28ms for the canary app.
maria chen: Nice. Can you paste the commands you ran so we can automate rollback?
ashok patel: Commands:
```
# flush stale
ip -6 neigh del 2001:db8:10::12 dev eth0
# pin via tunnel
ip -6 route replace 2001:db8:10::12/128 dev vxlan0
# confirm
ip -6 neigh show | grep 2001:db8:10::12
```
jin park: Long term we shouldn't be adding host /128s per pod. That workaround is ok for immediate recovery but we need root cause. I suspect: (1) CNI bug with neighbor garbage collection + (2) ToR NDP proxying. Also possible NIC firmware mis-sending gratuitous NAs after migration.
taylor nguyen: Another datapoint: Iperf6 between nodes shows MTU mismatch warnings on some paths. RDMA/RoCE clusters need jumbo 9000 but vxlan overhead wasn't accounted for. Could be fragments lost when jumbo vs 1500 mismatch.
ashok patel: Right — `ip link show` on offending hosts: one had mtu 9000 on eth0 but vxlan0 default 1500, so packets going through tunnel get fragmented. tcpdump saw ICMPv6 Packet too big messages dropped by intermediate.
maria chen: That could amplify the neighbor flaps if probes time out and retries go to other nodes. Can we standardize MTU for vxlan to 8972 (9000-UDP overhead) in CNI config?
jin park: Cilium has a setting for vxlan MTU (`vxlan-mtu`). We'll schedule a canary upgrade with vxlan-mtu tweak + neighbor GC fixes in Cilium 1.11 (fix referenced in their changelog).
sre-bot: Incident note: Created INC-2026-384 (network: us-west-2 ipv6 neighbor shadowing). Priority P2. Assigned to eng-infra.
deploy-bot: Rolling canary to ded-gpu-az-a-2 with vxlan-mtu=8972 and Cilium 1.11-rc1. Will watch 5 minutes.
ashok patel: Canary observed: no more duplicate neighbor entries for the pinned pod and p95 stayed <40ms over 10m. CPU on node unchanged.
taylor nguyen: Action items:
- short: apply neighbor flush script + route pinning as emergency playbook (ashok)
- mid: roll Cilium 1.11 with vxlan-mtu fix to ded pool (jin)
- infra: validate ToR NDP proxy config with netops to avoid split-horizon (maria)
- follow-up: run a network postmortem and include tests for ipv6 neighbor stability (owner: eng-infra)
jin park: Also need to audit NIC firmware batch (1.2.1 -> 1.2.3) — earlier firmware had a gratuitous-NA suppression bug.
maria chen: I'll open a ticket with netops for ToR proxy config. pinging @netops on the ticket.
ashok patel: Will attach tcpdumps and ip -6 neigh outputs to INC-2026-384. I'll also push the small bash neighbor-flush script to runbook repo.
jin park: FYI we saw a second symptom: kube-proxy IPVS was reprogramming services and flushing conntrack which temporarily made clients re-resolve neighbors and triggered a cascade. We'll include a note to avoid mass svc restarts during the rollout.
maria chen: Thanks everyone. If canary stays clean for 30m we'll schedule a controlled roll to ded-gpu-az-{0..3}.
ashok patel: Thanks. Postmortem draft assigned to me after stabilization. :thumbsup:
